goal: Help the developer create the correct Store submission package for a WinUI 3 app from the right project/template.
must_include: Notices the solution contains only the WinUI app project and no Windows Application Packaging Project or single-project MSIX Store packaging setup.

For the Visual Studio 2022/Windows App SDK 1.0-era fixture, recommends creating/using the `Blank App, Packaged with Windows Application Packaging Project` template or adding a Windows Application Packaging Project that references the app.

Tells them to run Package and Publish/Create App Packages from the packaging project (or the configured single-project MSIX project in newer tooling), not from an unrelated class library or unpackaged project.
Says Store submission should produce an `.msixupload`/`.appxupload` package upload file and that Partner Center will sign Store MSIX/AppX packages during submission.
must_not: Says WinUI 3 desktop apps cannot be published to the Microsoft Store.
Instructs them to upload the raw `bin\Release` executable folder as the Store package.
Requires buying a CA code-signing certificate for an MSIX/AppX Store submission.
acceptable_alternatives: Migrate the app to current single-project MSIX if the installed Visual Studio/Windows App SDK version supports Store package generation.
Use MSBuild packaging properties to generate a StoreUpload bundle in CI after the packaging project or single-project MSIX setup exists.
Create a new packaged-with-packaging-project WinUI solution and move the app code into it.
solved: The answer directs the developer to the packaging project or single-project MSIX Store packaging workflow and explains the `.msixupload`/Store signing outcome.
partial: The answer says to use Package and Publish but does not mention the missing packaging project/template or the Store upload artifact.
notes: Modern WinUI tooling can use single-project MSIX; because the fixture is VS 2022/Windows App SDK 1.0 with no packaging project, the accepted Stack Overflow fix remains applicable.
